doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: The Gold Fingers tour with ten pianists
summary: She toured Japan, Korea and China as the token woman in Gold Fingers with pianists including Hank Jones, Kenny Barron and Cedar Walton; she shares a connection with Roger Kellaway.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did I see you had a part in this “Hundred Fingers?”
Oh, Gold Fingers, yeah. Yeah ten piano players, we go to Japan every other year and they take what they call, what I heard, one token woman each time.

Yeah. And I think it was 1995, I guess that’s when it was, I was the token woman. That was great. It was great. We played quite a few concerts in Japan and we went to Korea and then I had my own concert in China, so I just made a nice little debut around there. It was great. We had Hank Jones and Kenny Barron and John Lewis. I’d never really hung out with these people, my idols from when I first started listening to music. And Cedar Walton, they put us together to do duos and it was a lot of fun. Junior Mance, the Blues Brothers, Ray Bryant, Roger Kellaway. I know I’m leaving — Barry Harris — I’m going to leave somebody out. Gene Harris.
I’d like to hear you and Roger together actually.
I think that would be quite something.

Oh yeah. Well we had some kind of — I don’t know whether you call it a metaphysical or — something that happened to me on an airplane. It was really bizarre. And I mentioned it to him and he couldn’t believe it because that had happened to him and then I couldn’t believe that could happen to anybody else. So we had that connection right away. I remember talking. I think he’ll remember it too, because it’s something you don’t run into. But they put him together with, was it Gene Harris? I think they would couple people together. So I was with Cedar. That’s what they liked. And I think they based some on the audience too, you know, with what the audience liked. And they had Roger with Gene Harris. So we didn’t stand a chance.
